meaning: The seven-note scale with a major third and a leading tone. It is the reading of an unmarked major key. Its M1 tier rests on 4 producer guides for dance and hip-hop use.
The seven-note minor scale with a flat third, flat sixth and flat seventh. It is the usual reading of minor in dance and hip-hop. Its M1 tier rests on 5 producer guides for dance and hip-hop use.
Five notes: root, minor third, fourth, fifth and flat seventh. No two neighbours sit a semitone apart.
Natural minor with a raised sixth. It sounds minor but less dark than natural minor. Its M1 tier rests on 5 producer guides for dance and hip-hop use.
Natural minor with a flat second, one semitone above the root. It is the darkest of the common minor sounds. Its M1 tier rests on 8 producer guides for dance and hip-hop use.
Major with a flat seventh. It keeps the major sound and drops the leading tone. Its M1 tier rests on 3 producer guides for dance and hip-hop use.
Natural minor with the seventh raised to a leading tone. That leaves a step and a half between the sixth and the seventh.
Phrygian with a major third. The flat second and major third give the common eastern or flamenco colour.
Major with a raised fourth. It sounds bright and floating. It stays M2: its 7 guides are general mood pages, not dance or hip-hop use.
Minor pentatonic plus the flat fifth, the blue note. It is the scale behind the word bluesy.
Five notes: root, major second, major third, fifth and major sixth.
Minor with a raised sixth and seventh, in the form used going up. Jazz players call it jazz minor.
Natural minor with a flat second and flat fifth. Its root chord is diminished. Its tier is M3: its 3 producer guides call it rare and name no dance or hip-hop use.
Major with a flat second and flat sixth. A step and a half follows each of them.
Harmonic minor with a raised fourth.
Six notes, each a whole step from the next. It has no perfect fifth and no sense of resolution.
Major pentatonic plus the flat third as a blue note.
Mixolydian plus a passing major seventh. The eight notes put chord tones on the beat when played in eighths.
Root, flat second, sharp second, major third, flat fifth, sharp fifth and flat seventh. Every tension of a dominant chord is altered.
Mixolydian with a raised fourth, or Lydian with a flat seventh.
Eight notes that alternate a half step and a whole step from the root. Players use it over a dominant chord.
Eight notes that alternate a whole step and a half step from the root. Players use it over a diminished chord.
Major with a flat sixth.
Dorian with a raised fourth.
Five notes: root, major second, minor third, fifth and flat sixth. Four books give four rotations, and this entry uses this one.
Five notes: root, flat second, fourth, fifth and flat seventh.
Eight notes: Phrygian with both the minor and the major third. It is the flamenco set, not the Spanish scale name.
All twelve pitch classes, so it keeps every note and filters none.
Five notes: root, major second, fourth, fifth and flat seventh, with no third. It shares its set with the slendro approximation.
Five notes: root, major second, fourth, fifth and major sixth, with no third or seventh.
Locrian with a natural sixth.
Major with a raised fifth.
Lydian with a raised second.
Locrian with a flat fourth and a doubly flat seventh. The oracle table lacks it, so only its degree string backs the set.
Dorian with a flat second.
Lydian with a raised fifth.
Mixolydian with a flat sixth.
Locrian with a natural second.
Root, raised second, major third, raised fourth, fifth, major sixth and flat seventh.
Root, flat second, major third, fourth, flat fifth, flat sixth and major seventh.
Harmonic minor with a flat second.
Melodic minor with a flat second.
Root, flat second, major third, then raised fourth, fifth and sixth, and a major seventh.
Locrian with a major second and major third. One library calls it arabian.
Root, flat second, major third, fourth, flat fifth, major sixth and flat seventh.
A seven-note North Indian raga set: flat second, flat third, raised fourth, fifth, flat sixth and major seventh.
Six notes: root, second, major third, raised fourth, major sixth and flat seventh, with no fifth.
Prometheus with a flat second.
Six notes that alternate a step and a half with a half step. Two augmented triads make it.
Five notes: root, minor third, fourth, flat sixth and flat seventh.
Five notes: root, major second, minor third, fifth and major sixth.
Five notes: root, flat second, fourth, flat fifth and flat seventh.
Five notes that fit one Javanese tuning into twelve equal steps. The real tuning is not twelve-tone.
Five notes that fit the five-tone gamelan tuning into twelve steps. The notes are off by 0, +40, -20, +20 and -40 cents.
Major plus a passing flat sixth, making eight notes.
Dorian plus a passing major third, making eight notes.
Natural minor plus a passing major seventh, making eight notes.
The Arabic maqam Hijaz on D, which equals Phrygian dominant exactly in twelve tones. Its second degree is a plain semitone, so nothing is lost.
The Arabic maqam Nahawand on C, which equals natural minor in twelve tones. The seventh may also rise to 11 at the top of a phrase.
The Arabic maqam 'Ajam, which equals the major scale in twelve tones.
The Arabic maqam Kurd on D, which equals Phrygian in twelve tones.
The Arabic maqam Nikriz on C, with a raised fourth and sixth over a minor third. Twelve tones hold it faithfully.
The Arabic maqam Rast on C, whose half-flat third and seventh round to major in twelve tones. The other rounding is 0 2 3 5 7 9 10, and the quarter tone is lost.
The Arabic maqam Bayati on D, whose half-flat second rounds up to a whole step here. The other rounding is 0 1 3 5 7 8 10, and the quarter tone is lost.
The Arabic maqam Sikah, which has no faithful twelve-tone set because it rests on quarter tones. No bend is written, so any twelve-tone stand-in loses them.
The Arabic maqam Saba, which has no faithful twelve-tone set because it rests on quarter tones. No bend is written, so any twelve-tone stand-in loses them.
Arabic as a scale name means Phrygian dominant. One library gives the name arabian to Locrian major, which this entry does not take.

default_pick.note: Take Phrygian dominant; take double harmonic major for very arabic or byzantine.

meaning: Very arabic or byzantine means double harmonic major, with its flat second and flat sixth.

default_pick.note: Take double harmonic major only when the request says very arabic or byzantine.

meaning: Gypsy minor means Hungarian minor, and a plain gypsy request takes it.

default_pick.note: Take Hungarian minor; gypsy major is double harmonic and spanish gypsy is Phrygian dominant.

meaning: Gypsy major means double harmonic major.

default_pick.note: Take double harmonic major only when the request says gypsy major.

meaning: Spanish gypsy means Phrygian dominant.

default_pick.note: Take Phrygian dominant only when the request says spanish gypsy.

meaning: Spanish as a scale name means Phrygian dominant, not the eight-note flamenco set.

default_pick.note: Take Phrygian dominant; take the eight-note set only when the request names flamenco or eight notes.

meaning: Egyptian without the word pentatonic means Hungarian minor.

default_pick.note: Take Hungarian minor; take the suspended pentatonic only when the request says pentatonic.

meaning: Egyptian pentatonic means the suspended five-note set with no third.

default_pick.note: Take the suspended pentatonic only when the request says pentatonic.

meaning: Pentatonic alone means minor pentatonic in a minor genre and major pentatonic otherwise. This entry is the minor reading.

default_pick.note: Take minor pentatonic in minor genres, else major pentatonic.

meaning: Pentatonic in a request for a major or non-minor genre means major pentatonic.

default_pick.note: Take major pentatonic when the genre is not minor.

meaning: Diminished as a scale name means the half-whole set when a dominant chord is present.

ask.question: Does diminished mean the half-whole or the whole-half scale?
ask.when: The request gives no chord context. Over a dominant chord the half-whole set is taken without asking.

default_pick.note: Take half-whole; take whole-half over a diminished chord.

meaning: Diminished over a diminished chord means the whole-half set.

default_pick.note: Take whole-half only over a diminished chord or when the request says whole-half.

meaning: Bebop minor can mean bebop Dorian, which adds a passing major third to Dorian.

ask.question: Does bebop minor mean bebop Dorian or bebop harmonic minor?
ask.when: The request says bebop minor with no mode word. A batch run takes bebop Dorian.

default_pick.note: Take bebop Dorian in a batch run.

meaning: Bebop minor can also mean bebop harmonic minor, which adds a passing major seventh to natural minor.

default_pick.note: Take bebop harmonic minor only when the request says so.

meaning: A request for a dark sound with no scale named. Evil or menacing asks for more, and mode is only one of six cues.

default_pick.note: Take natural minor and a lower register; take Phrygian for very dark, evil or menacing.

meaning: A bright or happy request. Listeners rated Lydian less happy than major, so Lydian suits airy better than happy.

default_pick.note: Take major; take Lydian for airy or floating.

meaning: A sad or melancholic request. Dorian reads as a less sad minor.

default_pick.note: Take natural minor; take Dorian for a less sad colour.

meaning: An uplifting request, where sources conflict. Trance and progressive styles use a minor key with a VI-VII loop, and other styles use major.

default_pick.note: Take natural minor with an i-VI-III-VII loop in trance and progressive styles, else major.

meaning: A dreamy request. A major-leaning sound takes Lydian, and a minor-leaning one takes Dorian with ninth chords.

default_pick.note: Take Lydian when the sound leans major, and Dorian with ninth chords when it leans minor.

meaning: An eastern, exotic or arabic request. Very arabic or byzantine asks for the double harmonic major scale.

default_pick.note: Take Phrygian dominant; take double harmonic major for very arabic or byzantine.

meaning: An epic or heroic request, where sources agree little. The pick is a natural minor loop in a wide register.

default_pick.note: Take natural minor with an i-bVI-bVII loop and a wide register.

meaning: A cinematic request that means drama: natural minor. This is the batch default.

ask.question: Should cinematic sound like wonder (Lydian) or drama (natural minor)?
ask.when: The request names no other mood or scale word. A batch run takes drama.

default_pick.note: Take natural minor for drama; ask first when the request names no other mood or scale word.

meaning: A cinematic request that means wonder: Lydian.

default_pick.note: Take Lydian only when the request says wonder or awe.

meaning: A bluesy request. A major sound uses Mixolydian instead.

default_pick.note: Take the minor blues scale; take Mixolydian for a major sound.

meaning: A jazzy request. It keeps the scale and adds seventh and ninth chords.

default_pick.note: Keep the scale already chosen and add seventh and ninth chords.

meaning: A tense or suspenseful request.

default_pick.note: Take Phrygian or harmonic minor.

meaning: A mysterious request, where sources conflict. Read the other mood and scale words in the request instead.

default_pick.note: Choose from the other words in the request.

meaning: A spooky or eerie request. Use few notes and accent the flat second or flat fifth.

default_pick.note: Take harmonic minor with few notes and accents on the flat second or flat fifth.

meaning: A euphoric request. Sources name no scale for it.

default_pick.note: No mapping: read the scale from the other words in the request.

meaning: Snapping keeps a note that lies in the scale and moves any other note to the nearer scale pitch, the lower on a tie. The rule shown is the E major case: 60 gives 59 and 61 stays.

An outside note passes when it lasts at most two sixteenths, falls off the beat, and is a passing or neighbour note between scale notes. Allow one per beat and one in eight notes, with passing notes between neighbours at most four semitones apart.
In a bluesy line on major, Mixolydian or pentatonic material, offsets 3, 6 and 10 may sit outside the scale. Each lasts at most one beat, and the next note is a scale tone one semitone away.
In a minor key, offset 11 may appear when the next note is the root a semitone above. Offset 9 may appear in an ascending run that reaches 11.

In 757 single-key pop songs the melody leaves the diatonic set in 0.27 percent of notes in major and 0.57 percent in minor. More than 1 percent is off-genre for pop, and jazz, blues and exotic requests have no data.
